newsitem.title: TURKEY: Procedure for Turkey's government handover.
newsitem.headline: Procedure for Turkey's government handover.

text.p: Here is the procedure for the planned transfer of power within Turkey's coalition government between Islamists and conservatives:
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan was to resign on Wednesday in an effort to swap jobs with his pro-Western coalition partner, Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller.
Islamist Erbakan would stay on as caretaker leader until President Suleyman Demirel named a party head to form a new administration.
Tradition dictates that Demirel choose the main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz, whose parliamentary strength is second only to Erbakan's Islam-based Welfare Party.
But Ciller, backed by the Islamists and probably by a far-right splinter party, may get the nod if she can offer the president the best chance of winning a confidence vote in parliament.

The prime minister-designate would then have 45 days to present Demirel with a cabinet list. Failure to do so would give the president the right to appoint his own multi-party government and order general elections within a further 90 days.
If Ciller were chosen, she would be expected to tell the president within a few days that she had formed a new government with Erbakan's Welfare Party.
Yilmaz, head of the conservative Motherland Party, would probably struggle to forge a coalition from among the rival secularist parties.
Any new government must face a confidence vote in parliament between five and ten days after informing Demirel of its formation.
The constitution does not specify how the vote should be carried out but the speaker's office says the government needs a majority of the votes cast in the 550-seat chamber.
